We are all different, that's a given. But we are more alike than it seems, at least at a fundamental level. I can't help but think that there are certain interests that create discord and animosity. These differences are often artificially created to sell more products or promote particular agendas.

There are certain cultures and environments that promote these artificial differences. Take politics, for example. We can choose from a variety of inclinations - conservatives, liberals, libertarians, socialists - but whatever flavor we may choose, if we think hard about it, we all really want the same basic stuff.

Following the political example, we all want to live a good life. We all want to be safe in our neighborhoods. We all want some kind of safety net when things go south or when we have a health scare. We all want our children to live in a better world. Now, how to obtain those goals, that is the difference. We can start a useful debate right there, and good ideas are going to come out. But do you really think that anyone disagrees with these basics? We are, essentially, agreeing in the back of our minds, and yet somehow we find ourselves fighting and arguing with each other like mad.

We are forced to choose between being A or being B, but it looks like we are all C instead.

# The vortex of options

There was a time when flying was a luxury item, but airlines started to open their price ranges to the public, and now we can travel almost everywhere at a reasonable price. However, initially, there were only two options: business and coach, the expensive and cheap seats. Nowadays, the number of flight classes has significantly increased, with options including Premium Economy, First Class, Economy Basic, Economy Plus, Premium Business, and Regional Business.

Some may argue that we don't need that many options. Comparing it to the evolution of dieting options, 30 years ago, there were fewer options than we have today. However, our nutrition needs are likely not fundamentally different. Similarly, Colgate currently offers over 20 different toothpaste options.

# Artificial differences

The point is that these differences are artificial, and someone created them to give us the illusion of choice. It is wise to stop and consider whether the multitude of options for a particular choice are genuinely necessary or whether most of them are just artificial.

Without falling into cynicism, I am going to contemplate this during the next political election. How many of the differences that politicians strongly emphasize are merely fabricated?

# Keeping you on your toes

Some companies create artificial conflicts, thinking that _keeping you on your toes_ will prevent distractions. It's important to be aware of this because a wolf that pretends to be friendly can be more dangerous than one that wears sheep's clothing.

# We all are C

The next time you find yourself arguing with someone online or at your workplace, reflect on what you genuinely desire and whether it is significantly different from the other person's desires. Shift the focus from A or B and try to find a common ground, look for C. Instead of being two people looking at each other, strive to be two people looking in the same direction.
